visible_text: Consider the following data: 19, 10, 12, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, m, n. If the mean and the median of the data are both 14, which of the following statements is correct? I. m ≥ 14; II. n ≤ 16; III. m + n = 30. Options: A. Only I and II; B. Only I and III; C. Only II and III; D. I, II, and III.
reasoning: Since there are exactly five numbers smaller than 14 in the known list (10,12,12,13,13), the median (the 6th value in the ordered 11‑element set) will be 14 only if both unknown values are at least 14; otherwise the count of numbers less than 14 would exceed five and the median would drop below 14. Hence I (m ≥ 14) holds, and by symmetry n ≥ 14 as well. The total sum must be 11·14 = 154. The sum of the known numbers is 19+10+12+12+13+13+14+15+16 = 124, so m + n = 154 − 124 = 30, giving III. With m ≥ 14 and m + n = 30, we have n = 30 − m ≤ 30 − 14 = 16, so II (n ≤ 16) also holds. Therefore all three statements are true, and the correct option is D.
